query: For HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy, stress–strain behavior, thermal expansion, and elastic behavior at elevated temperatures remain insufficiently understood. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain these responses? Define a controlled comparison, the observations predicted relative to a baseline state, the temperature and response limits within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, nano-scale B2-like Nb/Ta-rich chemical short-range order (CSRO) that survives fast quenching raises the Peierls barrier for ⟨111⟩ screw dislocations and reduces anharmonic lattice vibrations. Up to ≈1000 °C this CSRO therefore (i) suppresses thermal expansion, (ii) maintains a higher elastic modulus, and (iii) gives a yield-strength plateau. Above ≈1100 °C the CSRO progressively dissolves, eliminating these differences and producing rapid softening and a larger coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE).
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr single-phase BCC alloy, vacuum arc-melted, homogenised 1 h at 1200 °C and water-quenched to retain CSRO (oxygen <200 ppm).
generation.intervention: Incremental heating (in-situ) from 25 °C to 1400 °C under inert Ar while recording mechanical or dilatometric responses.
generation.conditions: Strain rate 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ s⁻¹ in compression or tension; heating/cooling rate ≤10 K min⁻¹; single-phase BCC (no oxides or precipitates).
generation.structural_mediator: Volume fraction and size (~1–2 nm) of B2-like Nb/Ta-rich CSRO clusters quantified by diffuse X-ray/neutron scattering Warren–Cowley parameters.
generation.mechanism: CSRO produces local lattice distortion that: (a) increases the Peierls stress for screw dislocation glide (solid-solution strengthening), and (b) stiffens interatomic bonds (lower Grüneisen parameter). When thermal energy exceeds the CSRO ordering enthalpy (≈1100 °C) the clusters disorder, removing these effects.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Relative to a fully random solid solution baseline:
1. Yield strength at 800 °C higher by ≥200 MPa; slope dσy/dT ≈0 between 600–1000 °C (strength plateau).
2. Dynamic Young’s modulus at 800 °C higher by ≥10 %.
3. CTE from 25–1000 °C lower by ≥10 %.
4. Differences in all three metrics fall below 5 % once T ≥1100 °C.
generation.baseline: Same alloy rendered fully random by 40 h anneal at 1400 °C followed by water quench (confirmed absence of CSRO).
generation.boundary: Temperature 25–1400 °C; strain to ≤5 %; no second-phase precipitation; oxygen <200 ppm.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude and stability range of CSRO may vary ±50 °C depending on minor impurity levels; predicted percentage differences may vary ±5 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimen sets: (A) CSRO-retaining (1200 °C/1 h/quake) and (B) random (1400 °C/40 h/quench). Verify CSRO by high-energy X-ray diffuse scattering and STEM. Measure (i) yield strength and modulus by compression tests at 25, 600, 800, 1000, 1200 °C, and (ii) CTE by push-rod dilatometry from 25–1400 °C, all in-situ.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if: (1) σy_CSRO − σy_random < +100 MPa or negative at 800 °C, (2) E_CSRO/E_random <1.05 at 800 °C, or (3) α_CSRO/α_random >0.95 below 1000 °C, provided CSRO is experimentally verified in set A and absent in set B.
